description: Given n processes with their IDs in pid and their parent process IDs in ppid, when you kill a process, all its child processes are also killed. Return a list of process IDs that will be killed given the kill target.
intuition: This is a tree traversal problem in disguise. Build a parent-to-children adjacency list, then BFS or DFS from the kill target. Every process you visit is a descendant that also gets killed, just like deleting a folder deletes everything inside it.
approach: Build an adjacency list (parent -> children) from pid and ppid. Use BFS/DFS starting from the kill target to find all descendant processes.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: pid=[1,3,10,5], ppid=[3,0,5,3], kill=5

Build childrenMap:
  ppid[0]=3: childrenMap.get(3)=[1]
  ppid[1]=0: childrenMap.get(0)=[3]
  ppid[2]=5: childrenMap.get(5)=[10]
  ppid[3]=3: childrenMap.get(3)=[1,5]

BFS from kill=5:
  queue=[5], killedProcesses=[]
  Dequeue 5: killedProcesses=[5], enqueue children [10] → queue=[10]
  Dequeue 10: killedProcesses=[5,10], no children
Return [5,10]
explanation:
1. Build a map from parent ID to list of child IDs.
2. Start BFS from the kill target.
3. For each process, add it to the result and enqueue its children.
4. Return all killed processes.
hints: Build a parent-to-children mapping for easy traversal.
Use BFS or DFS starting from the kill target.
All descendants of the killed process are also killed.
